Definition: from G5423; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude:--deceive.
BiblicalUsage: Phrenapatao means to deceive the mind, to delude oneself, and it appears once, in Paul's warning about pride. If a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that self-deception is the quietest sin: thinking I am something when I am nothing, and believing my own flattery.
